newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Swiss Re America on US strategy.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Swiss Re America on US strategy.

text.p: Swiss Re America, which considered making two separate U.S. acquisitions this summer, does not see any other likely candidates for a takeover in the United States.

Swiss Re America Chief Executive Officer Heidi Hutter told Reuters in a telephone interview that the company considered buying National Re Corp and American Re Corp, which were eventually purchased by Swiss Re rivals.
When asked whether Swiss Re America would still consider making a U.S. acquisition, Hutter said: "In principle, yes; but in practice, who?
"In terms of other acquisitions, we don't really see anything," she said.
However, she said she believes there will be more consolidation in the reinsurance industry.
"If you look at the broker market reinsurers I think there is a lot of room for combinations that would make sense," she said.
Swiss Re America's parent, Swiss Reinsurance Co, on Tuesday agreed to buy Mercantile & General Re from Britain's Prudential Corp Plc for about $2.27 billion.
That deal was part of a strategic initiative that she believed began before it considered making offers for National Re and American Re, she said.
Swiss Re's interest in M&G Re, she said, was not in reaction to General Re Corp 's purchase of National Re or Munich Re's buyout of American Re.
"We had been in a due diligence for M&G Re for a long time," Hutter said.
And the deal will make it the world's largest life and health reinsurer, she said.
But the M&G purchase does little to boost its position in the United States, where analysts say Swiss Re now faces a tougher competitive battle following this summer's merger wave.
In July, General Re, the largest reinsurer in the United States, bought National Re for $940 million.
A few weeks later, Munich Re, the world's largest reinsurer responded by buying American Re for $3.3 billion.
Those deals solidified General Re's top spot in the U.S. market and vaulted Munich Re into second place.
Although American Re was a prime property, some analysts have speculated that Swiss Re may have been unwilling to pay such a rich price for it.
"I think they paid a very full price," Hutter said of Munich Re's deal for American Re.
But Swiss Re now ranks fourth in a market where larger reinsurers increasingly wield a competitive edge over smaller rivals, analysts say.

Hutter said Swiss Re America, which moved to a client segment focus in March, plans to continue putting its efforts into improving its ongoing operations rather than pursuing frantic, and possibly foolhardy, growth.

"I'm really trying to make sure we focus in Swiss Re America on getting better because I'm convinced that if we focus on getting better, then in time we will get bigger and will attract more business," Hutter said.
"But if I focus on getting bigger, then I know I'll get worse," she said.
Indeed, Hutter said she was willing to scale back some of the company's premium volume in a shift away from pro rata to more selective and more profitable excess of loss business.
And Swiss Re has seen its combined ratio drop to 104.1 percent in the first six months of 1996 compared to 105.8 percent, excluding an asbestos and environmental reserving action, in 1995.
The combined ratio indicates whether a company is earning a profit on the business it writes. An underwriting profit occurs when the ratio is below 100 percent.

"That's what I call fundamental improvement in the book of business," she said. Swiss Re America added $700 million to reserves for asbestos and environmental liabilities in 1995 and Hutter said those reserves still appear to be sufficient.

Meanwhile, she said Swiss Re's business in the United States is much larger than many people realize because some of the business is handled from Europe and it has a substantial life reinsurance business its competitors don't have.

"I think it under portrays Swiss Re as a total entity" she said of the figures used in ranking their business, "because we as a group have much better diversity in terms of our product lines and geography than any of our other leading competitors."

And as part of its client segment focus, it will continue to work to streamline internal operations and improve customer service by bolstering its global and national, regional and specialty, and alternative risk transfer businesses.
Hutter also said she sees further development of Swiss Re America's marine and engineered risk business.
